question: What is the main medical use of antidepressant medications?

options.A: Lowering high blood pressure in pregnancy

explanation: Antidepressants are medications used to help stabilize mood and ease symptoms of depression and anxiety. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is it important for midwives to know about antidepressant therapy?

options.A: Midwives must replace the role of psychiatric specialists completely
options.B: Midwives diagnose all complex mental health disorders in labor
options.C: Midwives frequently care for pregnant women experiencing psychological distress
options.D: Midwives are legally required to prescribe psychiatric medications

explanation: Knowing about these treatments helps midwives support expectant mothers, watch for side effects, and connect them with the right care team. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which brain chemical is the main target for Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)?
explanation: SSRIs work by blocking the reabsorption of serotonin, which keeps more of it active in the brain. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h2)

question: How do SNRIs differ from standard SSRIs?

options.A: SNRIs have no effect on neurotransmitter levels at all
options.B: SNRIs only work on dopamine receptors in the brain
options.C: SNRIs are exclusively used for treating high blood pressure
options.D: SNRIs affect both serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake

explanation: Unlike SSRIs which focus only on serotonin, SNRIs target two different brain chemicals at the same time. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h2)

question: When are antidepressants usually considered during pregnancy?

options.A: Normal physiological fatigue of late pregnancy
options.B: Mild transient mood changes after delivery
options.C: Acute physical pain during the first stage of labor
options.D: Moderate to severe major depressive disorder

explanation: Doctors usually recommend these medications when depression is moderate to severe and talking therapies alone are not enough. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is a major risk of leaving severe depression untreated during pregnancy?

options.A: Immediate spontaneous closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus
options.B: Rapid increase in maternal production of oxytocin
options.C: Permanent cessation of all normal postpartum lactation
options.D: Impaired maternal-infant bonding and poor antenatal care

explanation: Untreated severe depression can make it hard for a mother to look after her health and connect with her baby. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h3)

question: How do most antidepressant medications reach the growing fetus during pregnancy?

options.A: By traveling upward from the maternal vagina
options.B: By direct absorption through the amniotic fluid
options.C: By synthesis within the fetal liver

explanation: Antidepressants can easily pass through the placenta and enter the baby's bloodstream. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h4)

question: A newborn whose mother took high-dose SSRIs right up until birth looks a bit jittery and feeds poorly. What is the most likely cause?

options.B: Severe neonatal bacterial sepsis from labor
options.C: An acute overdose of maternal oxytocin

explanation: Babies exposed to these drugs late in pregnancy can show mild, temporary withdrawal signs that go away on their own. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h4)

question: When do the physical side effects of new antidepressants usually feel the strongest?

options.A: Before the very first tablet is swallowed
options.B: Only after the medication is completely stopped
options.C: After exactly six months of continuous use
options.D: During the first two weeks of treatment

explanation: Side effects are most noticeable right after starting the medication, before the body gets used to it. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which symptom needs urgent attention when caring for a patient who just started an antidepressant?

options.A: A slight decrease in overall appetite
options.B: Emerging thoughts of self-harm or suicide
options.C: Mild dry mouth and temporary daytime fatigue

explanation: In the early days of starting treatment, some patients may experience an increase in dark thoughts, which needs immediate medical evaluation. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which antidepressant is known for passing into breast milk in very small amounts?
explanation: Sertraline is frequently chosen during breastfeeding because very little of the medication passes into the milk. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h6)

question: What should a midwife look out for when a breastfed baby's mother takes an antidepressant?

options.A: Assessing the infant's natural blood pressure
options.B: Measuring exact daily weight gain to the gram
options.C: Checking for early primary tooth eruption
options.D: Detecting signs of unusual sedation or poor feeding

explanation: Watching the baby for unusual sleepiness or trouble feeding helps catch any rare side effects early. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h6)

question: How long does it usually take for antidepressants to start improving a patient's mood?
explanation: Brain chemistry takes time to adjust, so noticeable mood improvements usually appear after a few weeks. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h7)

question: Why do some patients stop taking their antidepressants during the first week?

options.A: The medication cures the underlying depression instantly
options.B: Therapeutic benefits make them forget to take the pills
options.C: Side effects appear immediately before any mood relief is felt
options.D: Local clinics run out of supply within twenty-four hours

explanation: Patients often feel the side effects right away, but have to wait weeks for the mood benefits, which can make them want to quit early. [learn more](BMP223_U4_T2#BMP223_U4_T2_h7)
